task: model a part in parametric CAD software (Fusion 360, Onshape, Tinkercad, SketchUp, FreeCAD, Shapr3D): pick a plane and draw a sketch, constrain and dimension it so the geometry is defined rather than eyeballed, turn it into a solid by extruding or revolving, add the features the part needs — fillets, chamfers, holes, shells, patterns — measure or check fit against the dimensions it has to hit, and export it for manufacture as STL, STEP, or a dimensioned drawing; complete when the export completes or the finished part is shown fully defined. Surface pinned: the modelling session on one part. This domain differs from the rest of the creative set in that the work has a correctness condition, not only a look: a dimension is right or wrong, a sketch is fully constrained or it is not, and parts either fit or they do not. Capture that. Off-task: rendering, materials and lighting passes, animation or exploded-view videos, digital sculpting for art (Blender, ZBrush), slicer-only walkthroughs that start from a downloaded STL, 3D-printer reviews and calibration, and software overviews that never build one part.

tree.label: Model and export a CAD part
tree.note: 1 first, and its units and its component constrain everything after. 2 wherever the part has to match something real, which is eight of the seventeen, and it can run before the first sketch or in the middle. then 3, 4 and 5 as one loop, once per feature: rglv runs it three times, N3Dw eight. 6 as the part needs, and 6.11 wherever one feature has to repeat. 7 whenever an earlier value turns out wrong, which is every parametric video and none of the three SketchUp ones. 8 when there is something to check against, and 9 last. LVhh, YFgd and zmd0 never reach 9 at all, and A5bc stops before 6 and says so.

children.label: Set up the modelling session
children.note: 1.9 first where the tool is not on the machine yet, which is rglv alone. then 1.1 and 1.2 before any geometry, in that order - A5bc, 4G2E, 6yPK, d3qG, zmd0 and N3Dw all set the units first, and pMWn instead attaches a unit to each dimension in 4.4. 1.3 where the tutorial wants a known starting state. 1.4 and 1.5 before the first sketch in the course videos and never in the SketchUp ones. 1.6, 1.7 and 1.8 whenever the screen gets in the way, and they are revisited: LVhh runs 1.8 four times and YFgd runs it at the end for the final shot.

questions.question: Did the export actually produce a file, or is it still queued?
questions.why: Many modern CAD tools process STEP or complex exports in the cloud, meaning the file isn't immediately available and the job can silently fail or get stuck pending.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate confirmation that the manufacturing file was actually generated successfully rather than just sent to a stalled server queue.
questions.check: does the export status show completed, or still pending/queued
questions.say_example: That export's still showing pending. Give it a moment before assuming the file's there.
